title: Camillus de Lellis (mid-July)
hookLine: a gambler and soldier who founded nursing brothers with red crosses on their habits

cards: A young man with a bad leg and a worse habit. He's been a soldier for hire, fighting wherever there's pay. Between wars he plays cards and dice, and he loses.
Tradition says he once gambled away nearly everything he owned, down to the shirt on his back.

To eat, he works as a laborer, then as an attendant in a Roman hospital, the kind of place for people nobody expects to get well. He's dismissed for gambling. So how does that man end up founding an order of nurses?

teach.b: Camillus de Lellis didn't turn around all at once. Tradition says the change began while he worked as a laborer for Capuchin friars, when one of them took him aside and spoke to him plainly about his life.
He was taken in as a novice, but the wound on his leg, which never healed, opened again, and the friars sent him away.

teach.h: BACK TO THE HOSPITAL, TO STAY.
teach.b: So he went back to the hospital, and this time he stayed. He watched how the sick were treated: hired attendants who didn't care, patients left dirty, hungry, alone.
He began to gather a few men who would nurse the sick the way a mother nurses her only child, a picture tradition gives in his own words.
That little group became an order, called the Ministers of the Infirm, and Camillus became a priest. Then came the red cross.

teach.h: A RED CROSS ON A BLACK HABIT.
teach.b: His brothers wore a large red cross on the chest of their black habits, so anyone, in a ward or a street, could see who had come to serve. They went into hospitals, into the homes of the dying, onto battlefields.
Under all of it was the Gospel scene of the last judgment, where Jesus counts care for the sick as care done to himself.
For Camillus, that was not a figure of speech: the patient in the bed was Christ. And the old gambler kept something from his past. He never stopped taking risks.

teach.h: HE CHANGED WHAT HE BET ON.
teach.b: He just changed what he bet on.

how: Catholics honor Saint Camillus de Lellis in mid-July as a patron of the sick, nurses and hospitals, and his order, the Camillians, still serves the sick wearing the red cross.

games.q: you're Camillus. the friars have sent you away over your bad leg. what do you do?
o: go back to the hospital and stay.
games.why: he went back to the hospital he'd been dismissed from, and stayed. that's where the order began.

practice: Go back to a time you were sick or hurt, a hospital bed, a fever at home, a long recovery, and find the one who took care of you: a nurse whose name you never learned, a parent, a friend who brought soup.
Stay with their hands and their voice, and what they did that you couldn't. If you pray, thank God for them and ask a blessing on their work; if you don't, hold them in gratitude.
